key_insight: Structured environmental noise can make photon loss Fock-state dependent, pushing bosonic logical states outside the nominally correctable error space.
engineering_relevance: Bosonic quantum error correction should account for realistic environmental spectra and state-dependent dissipation rather than assume an ideal photon-loss operator.
method: Inject spectrally engineered noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator in a 3D circuit-QED system.
Measure Fock-state dynamics and compare with second-order time-convolutionless theory.
Apply narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit to probe error-space deformation.
evidence_signal: Measured dynamics showed frequency-selective loss and non-Markovian transients consistent with theory, while narrowband noise drove encoded states beyond the nominally correctable error space.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify logical error-rate penalties under naturally occurring environmental noise.
paper_title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
